# Introduction {#sec-preprocess .unnumbered}

As a first step after importing the data into
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("TreeSummarizedExperiment")`, one should explore
the data and perform quality control (QC). This is important because data
quality affects the final results, and failing to assess it accurately can
lead to erroneous interpretations. QC and exploration are discussed in
[@sec-quality-control].

Based on the QC results, researchers usually apply sample and feature
filtering to improve the robustness of the analysis. To focus on a
specific taxonomic rank, data agglomeration is commonly performed.
Filtering and agglomeration are discussed in detail in
[@sec-treese_subsetting] and [@sec-agglomeration].

Data transformations, covered in [@sec-assay-transform], are applied after
filtering. For more information on preprocessing, you can refer to
@Zhou2023, for instance.

@fig-preprocess-steps summarises the typical order of these steps; click a
step to open its chapter.

```{mermaid}
%%| label: fig-preprocess-steps
%%| fig-cap: "Typical preprocessing steps between data import and downstream analysis."
flowchart LR
    imp["Import<br/>into TreeSE"] --> qc["Explore &<br/>quality control"]
    qc --> sub["Filter samples<br/>& features"]
    sub --> agg["Agglomerate<br/>to a rank"]
    agg --> tr["Transform"]
    tr --> ana["Downstream<br/>analysis"]
    classDef step fill:#e6f3f7,stroke:#0087af,color:#070707
    classDef ends fill:#ffffff,stroke:#6c757d,color:#070707
    class qc,sub,agg,tr step
    class imp,ana ends
    click imp "import.html" "Importing data"
    click qc "quality_control.html" "Exploration & quality control"
    click sub "subsetting.html" "Subsetting"
    click agg "agglomeration.html" "Agglomeration"
    click tr "transformation.html" "Transformation"
```
